title: King's Gambit: the ideas
line: White gives a pawn to build the center and open a file for the rook.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your king two squares. It takes space in the center and frees your queen and a bishop.

also.d2d4: Pushing the queen's pawn is also sound and leads to other openings. This lesson pushes the king's pawn.

steps.text: Push the pawn on f2 two squares. It offers itself for Black's pawn on e5, to open the file for your rook.

also.g1f3: The knight move is the most common here, also sound, and leads to the Italian Game, the Ruy Lopez and others. This lesson offers the pawn.
also.b1c3: That is the Vienna Game, also sound. This lesson offers the pawn.
also.f1c4: That is the Bishop's Opening, also sound. This lesson offers the pawn.

steps.after: The King's Gambit. Engines rate it a little worse than the knight move and masters seldom play it, but it gives sharp games.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. It keeps the black queen from giving check on h4.

also.f1c4: That is the Bishop's Gambit, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out.

steps.after: Black strikes back in the center with a pawn.

steps.text: Take the pawn on d5. Black gives it to free its pieces, and you are a pawn up for now.
steps.after: Black's knight attacks your pawn on d5.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out to guard the pawn on d5. It aims at f7 as well.

also.f1b5: The bishop check is also sound. This lesson goes to c4.

steps.after: The knight takes back on d5. It guards the pawn on f4.

steps.text: Castle. Your rook lands on the file the gambit opened.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It takes the center and opens a line for your bishop toward f4.
Take the knight on d5. It was the last guard of the pawn on f4.
Now take back the pawn on f4 with your bishop.
steps.after: Material is level. You have a pawn in the center and your pieces are out.

summary: White gives a side pawn, castles onto the file it opened, and wins the pawn back once its guard is gone.
